A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, including tuning-bias comparisons and sensitivity studies in Sections 3–5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classification experiments and adds original regression experiments on the Protein Structure dataset in Appendix C, Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The tuning procedures, objectives, and order-preserving constraint are retained. The new vector- and matrix-scaling characterizations explain the existing constraint; they do not establish an altered algorithm. Regression extends evaluation of the data-reuse principle.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates image classification on three benchmarks. v2 retains these and adds Protein Structure regression using conformalized quantile regression, substantially extending empirical coverage to continuous outcomes and prediction intervals.

E2.justification: The classification comparisons retain RAPS, SAPS, score aggregation, temperature scaling, vector scaling, C-Adapter, and ConfTr, including ConfTr with and without order preservation. The regression study compares the existing same-data and hold-out strategies; the newly cited Liang et al. work is not evaluated as an additional competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a regression protocol using quantile random forests and 90% target coverage. It varies candidate counts from 40 to 200 at n = 50, then varies n from 100 to 500 with 200 candidates, reporting interval length alongside coverage measures. Hold-out uses 2n reserved observations versus n for reuse. Existing classification settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 add controlled regression sensitivity studies of candidate-pool complexity and calibration-set size. These extend the scaling-law investigation beyond classification and test finite model selection rather than only the existing parameter-freezing analysis. The original classification sensitivities and regularization comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 gains uncertainty values alongside previously reported point estimates. Both versions already describe 30 repetitions and mean/standard-deviation reporting; the new regression study also uses 30 independent runs. There is no documented increase in repetitions for existing experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 add regression coverage, interval-length, coverage-gap, and tuning-bias results; candidate-count bias is nonmonotonic. In Table 1, ConfTr with order preservation changes from 0.04%/0.02% to 0.52%/0.40% on CIFAR-100/ImageNet, now exceeding unchanged temperature-scaling values of 0.14%/0.04%. Unregularized ConfTr changes from 5.5%/21.3% to 6.15%/21.68%. Existing plotted classification values are retained.

T1.justification: The central bounds and existing proofs are retained. Appendix K adds Lemma K.1 characterizing order-preserving vector scaling, with a proof, and Lemma K.3 characterizing matrix scaling as W = aI + 1v^T with constant bias. These provide specific parameter-space refinements; Lemma K.3 has no accompanying proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about negligible bias for simple tuning, scaling with complexity and calibration size, theoretical bounds, and mitigation through reduced complexity. The additions support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting class counts to tuning complexity and interpreting C-Adapter through constrained matrix scaling. Remark 2.4 expands the practical rationale for data reuse. Appendix C interprets regression findings as similar to the main trends, although Table 2 does not consistently support increasing bias with candidate count. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and documents the regression dataset dimensions, quantile-forest package, candidate-grid construction, and reserved-data allocation. These are new reproducibility disclosures; the existing classification implementation details in Appendix A are effectively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liang, Zhu, and Barber (2024), Conformal prediction after efficiency-oriented model selection, as the basis for the regression setup. Existing research positioning is largely retained, with a modest expansion of the general-learnability framing.

P1.justification: v2 expands the background and practical motivation, rewrites parts of the empirical discussion, adds a regression appendix and acknowledgements, and adjusts notation. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact; appendix renumbering does not represent removed material.

P2.justification: v2 adds two regression tables and reformats Table 1 for uncertainty values and column-level percentage units. Figure 2(a) and two Figure 3(d) panels receive revised labels and legends; the latter also lose dataset headings. Their plotted values are unchanged, and the overall visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The regression study broadens evidence beyond v1's classification experiments, while Table 1 uncertainties and the code link improve transparency. The added order-preserving characterizations make the mitigation discussion more concrete. These gains are limited by Appendix C's overly confirmatory interpretation of nonmonotonic candidate-count results and the absence of a proof for Lemma K.3.
